<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Vaughan, 27 Oct: pij-rs cannot send files to Telegram, which is 'stupid'; 'I thought it did'. The deep look (2026-10-27) found it did, briefly: PR #49 (ce2721d) added `pij-rs sidecar telegram --file` and `pij send pij-telegram --file` as Telegram documents, was green in CI and live-canaried on this machine, but was never reviewed or merged, so later bounces from main dropped it. It is 100 commits behind with one doc conflict. Main is text-only (docs/how/pij-telegram.md says so), the shim refuses --file, and inbound media from Vaughan is discarded with no event. The old TS bridge (pij-poc e5dd811) sent photos/animations/documents by extension and saved inbound media to the session's attachments dir. This plan restores #49 and closes the gaps the brief names. Prime rulings: assets/rulings.md.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- An agent can hand Vaughan an image, video, GIF or any file through pij, and it arrives as the right kind of Telegram message.
- Nothing is dropped silently, in either direction.
- The bot token can never leak through the media path.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Deploying: no relink, daemon restart, extension reload, or live canary without Vaughan's go.
- Saving inbound media to disk (follow-up issue, ac-0008).
- sendMediaGroup albums: they cannot mix documents with photos/videos and prevent per-file fallback.
- Several files through the `pij send` shim; it stays one --file, no body, as #49 shipped it.
- Retention of staged copies after a terminal failure (#49 keeps them; noted for the follow-up).

| ac-0001 | Restore #49. Commit ce2721d (pij-fleet#49, Vaughan Knight, 13 Oct) is cherry-picked onto main 26fc3ba with its authorship and trailers kept; the one textual conflict (docs/how/pij-rs-api.md) is resolved keeping main's watchdog line and #49's --file line; #49's own tests (sidecar telegram_document_tests, daemon shim_http, CLI sidecar_producer, arch_drift) pass on the new base. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0002](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0002 | Method by type. Staging classifies each file by its lower-cased extension and size, and the job records the method: jpg/jpeg/png/webp up to 10 MB -&gt; sendPhoto (field `photo`); a larger image -&gt; sendDocument; mp4 -&gt; sendVideo (field `video`); gif -&gt; sendAnimation (field `animation`, ruling Q2); anything else -&gt; sendDocument. When sendPhoto, sendVideo or sendAnimation answers HTTP 400, the same attempt re-sends the same staged bytes with sendDocument; the 400 is recorded as telegram.outbound-delivery-failed carrying `method` and `fallback: sendDocument`. A delivered file appends telegram.outbound-media-delivered with the method used, file name, size and sha256. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0004](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0003 | Several files. `pij-rs sidecar telegram --file &lt;p&gt; [--file &lt;p&gt; ...]` accepts up to 10 files. The daemon stages every file before queueing any; if one is refused, nothing is queued and copies already staged are removed. Each file is its own job (per-file outcome in pij.sqlite; a retry never resends a delivered file), queued in argument order on the chat's serial key, so they arrive in order. With one file and no body the file keeps the request msg_id; otherwise file n uses `&lt;msg_id&gt;#&lt;n&gt;`. --caption goes on the first file; every file's caption carries the [sender] tag. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0004](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0004 | Body with files. --body or --body-file may be combined with --file. The body is queued first as an ordinary text send (same prefix, chunking and failure events as today), then the files. Without --file the text path is unchanged. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0004](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0005 | Refuse before sending. The CLI resolves each --file to an absolute path and fails on a missing one; the daemon re-checks and refuses, before anything is queued: a missing, unreadable, empty or non-regular file; a file over 50 MB (52,428,800 bytes); a caption over 1024 characters behind the sender tag; a relative path; more than 10 files. Job payloads record the source path, staged path, file name, size, sha256 and method, never the bytes. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0005](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0006 | Redaction. The bot token never appears in a job payload, a job's failure outcome, a spine event, or the error the worker logs, on any media path: transport failure, HTTP error status, ok=false, and the 400 fallback. The token is never on the CLI's argv (it lives only in the daemon's credential file). Proved with a sentinel token against a fake Bot API, plus a mutant that formats the raw reqwest error. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0005](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0007 | Inbound media is not dropped silently (ruling Q3b). Today handle_update ignores any message without text, caption included. An allowed user's photo, document, video, animation, audio, voice, video_note or sticker is now delivered to the bound seat as a text turn: `[telegram media not saved by pij-rs: &lt;kind&gt;, &lt;size&gt;, &lt;file name&gt;] caption: &lt;caption&gt;`, and appends telegram.inbound-media-unsupported (update_id, conversation, kind, size, file name, msg_id). With no binding it is refused exactly as text is. Text handling is unchanged. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0005](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
